body: **2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded** (rx3cmhmn, §8) — `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` gained the MCP call deadline, and `+ contract/instance-unreachable-detail/call-deadline` added call-deadline as the seventh MCP-only unreachable cause. The CLI's exit-21 set stays six, and the outcome of a send is unknown. This chunk's paste bound has to fit under that 55 s deadline. If it adds its own closed word, the word extends this register and the time-bounds list the same way.

**2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded** (4urjbp6k, §8) — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` gained the MCP call deadline. This is the direct precedent: a new bound viola holds is added to this list, and the entry states whom it falls on. The paste bound must fall on the driver and must never block, refuse or delay a key.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — Set the readiness gate's `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s), which ends in not-delivered / input-not-ready with nothing typed. The bound falls on the driver only. A key pressed during the wait takes the wheel and the send is refused human-typing. The rule is "the human always wins" through a wait of seconds. The outer-PTY case `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins` is sequenced on records, never on a timer, and its stated limit is that it cannot tell send's first wheel read from its second. This is the template for what human keys do while a paste is blocked or after it is cut. It also gives the gate's bound that the paste bound's arithmetic must count.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — Added the confirm windows `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s) and `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s), which end in not-delivered / no-prompt-submitted, a bound on the driver only with the wheel untouched. These windows count in send's total against the MCP call deadline. A cut paste that leaves text with no Enter meets this confirmation path.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — MCP `wait` clamps to `WAIT_CAP` 50 s, a driver-only bound that sits below the client's tool-call timeout. It is a precedent for keeping viola's bounds below the MCP client's limit, and for a driver-only bound that touches no key and leaves the wheel alone.

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** — The first entry to put a time bound on the driver and never on the human (§8 Timeout extensions). On expiry viola fails open and the vendor TUI is left to the human. It sets the pattern this chunk's bound follows.

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — Made the dialog hold configurable and kept it on the driver: any human key still hands the dialog back at once, whatever the hold. No human-facing time limit was added, which keeps `absence/user-time-limit` and `decision/no-unwarned-timeouts` intact. A paste bound must not add one either.

**2026-11-15-live-round-on-the-trimmed-product** — `~ decision/dialog-hold-bounds-the-driver` moved to standing after a live measurement. The precedent: a bound applied ahead of ratification stays provisional until it is measured.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — Added the 5 s `claude agents --json` read. It fails open and falls on viola's own child, never on a key. This is the "agents read" member of the time-bounds rows the chunk extends.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** — Added `STATUSLINE_DEADLINE` and stated whom it falls on, because the plan lists every bound viola holds and whom it falls on. The bound was later retired, but this is the origin of the register that a paste bound joins.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** — The budget pause was a driver-only refusal of send with exit 11 and nothing typed, and its keyboard case read that a human key reaches the child while no `unable`, `hint:` or code reaches the outer PTY. The exit is now retired (`contract/cli-exit-codes/11`). It is a precedent for a new send refusal word, and a warning not to reuse exit 11.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** (cjoqaris, §8) — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` dropped the budget pause. This is the row the paste bound will join.

body: A new compiled time bound on the paste into the child, a time bound that must fall on the driver only and never on the human at the keyboard.

The send's ending at the paste bound: a closed code word from the closed refusal, detail or cause sets, never upstream or vendor text and never a bare error or stack trace, with the same word on the CLI send and the MCP send tool.

The CLI refusal output of send at the bound: the unable line with its reason code, the hint line (one hint per code), the exit code, and the one clean --json failure document with no hint; a fault, if it is one, carries no hint.

If a new closed word is added, it joins the closed code-word sets in the code-word format, with its fixed copy taken from design, its hint, and a writer and a witness for its error body; unlisted code words stay visible.

The MCP send tool's result at the bound, read against the MCP call deadline (55 s) and its expiry detail call-deadline: the paste bound plus the rest of send stays under it, so the driver no longer reads call-deadline with the outcome unknown.
The wheel stays unmoved when the paste is cut: the bound's ending is no take of the wheel, and only a human key takes it.
The human's keystrokes are never blocked behind a paste that is stuck on the child, during the block and after the cut; send stays refused while the human types.

The cut paste's residue in the child's input box (text without Enter) and what the next send meets there: the send refusals input-not-ready and no-prompt-submitted, the confirmation, and never presumed delivered.
Zero viola bytes on the terminal: cutting the paste writes nothing of the wrapper's own to the human's terminal, and any diagnostic of the cut goes off the terminal.
The TUI passthrough contracts the paste path crosses: human keystrokes and viola terminal bytes, the boundary check never inspecting claude content beyond signatures.
The measuring child is the fake agent with a behaviour that stops reading its PTY; boundary tests are sequenced on records, and no live reading of a real claude gates anything.
The CLI exit codes the send path can end with at the bound, including exit 21 with its instance-unreachable detail under --json.

Zero flakiness and no retries: the intermittent rig rehearsal red is acted on only at its next red, its cause read first, with no retry rule and no loosened entry; every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint.

every fixed CLI string a new refusal prints is pinned by its literal in a test, the refusal layout held by those pins
a11y failures are nextest failures that fail the build, with zero flakiness and no retries

body: The viola list board and its caption, stale-row escapes, NAME truncation and the amber and bold SGR rules: the chunk does not touch the board.
viola link and unlink, plugin install, viola revive and its --list and --json refusals, and the start refusals of run, revive and verify: none sits on the send path.
viola verify interrupted, viola wait output and its timed_out, the MCP wait tool's timeout_ms, and the dialog hold, its config and dialog-expired event.
viola --help rows: group labels, usage line, handoff row and served verbs.
Screen-reader targets and setups, the manual keyboard and Orca passes: they gate nothing and the chunk adds no manual reading.
The absences of a web or graphical frontend, a touch surface, internationalization and a rendered page, and the N/A harness areas (contrast, focus management, WCAG mapping).
Hook event and dialog calls and their socket-directory, strict-modes and server-verify refusals before any frame.

**2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded** (Established Decisions, Conventions, the two later rows) — added `decision/mcp-call-deadline`: a compiled 55 s deadline above the 50 s wait cap, with expiry `call-deadline`. It grew `contract/unreachable-cause/cause-set` to seven causes, `call-deadline` written by MCP alone, and added `call-deadline` to `decision/mcp-unreachable-result-for-every-cause` as a cause found after a frame is sent. It also rewrote `decision/send-time-bound`: «on the MCP surface the MCP call deadline bounds the driver's wait, never the send itself». It names the false clause directly: the old total-under-client-timeout claim «is false while the paste write has no time bound … the paste's gap is the route's CARRY». This chunk discharges that CARRY. The paste bound has to fit the arithmetic against `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE` that these rows set up.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** (/compact's 40 s window) — added `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` = 40 s (`decision/compact-confirm-window`) beside the 10 s window, `SendSlot::window()` being the one bound. It stated that a compact send's blocking total is 48.5 s plus the paste, under an MCP ceiling read at 50 012 ms. This is the longest send total that the paste bound has to be added to while staying below the 55 s deadline, and «plus the paste» is the unbounded term.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — raised `GATE_MAX_WAIT` to 8.5 s (`decision/gate-timings-compiled`, `decision/send-waits-out-paste-hint`) and set send's longest block at 18.5 s (8.5 + 10). It added the second wheel/turn read after the gate (`contract/refusal-order/send`). Trap it recorded: a case that reads a verified literal-less screen through a clock that never advances waits forever. A paste-bound test using a test clock meets the same hazard.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** (the MCP tools' contract) — set the MCP `wait` cap at 50 s and recorded the client's tool-call timeout as above 50 s, «above the 18.5 s send total». It also defined `-32603` for an internal handler fault and the `isError` shapes (`contract/mcp-tool-errors/-32603`, `contract/mcp-tool-results/*`). The MCP `send` tool's result at the paste bound has to fit these shapes.

**2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records** — introduced `send-issued`, `send-confirmed` and `send-refused`, and the rule that «a paste failing after `send-issued` is `input-not-ready` with its cursor» (`contract/send/paste-failure-after-issue`). It added viola-pty's `PasteHandle` and `validate_paste_text`, and the gate tee's `sync_channel(256)` + `try_send`, which drops and poisons rather than blocking (`decision/passthrough-never-waits-on-model`). This is the standing outcome for a failed paste: a cut paste either reuses it or the chunk has to amend it.

**2026-11-16-send-confirmation** (Established Decisions) — added `decision/send-flight-lock`: the post-gate reads, the link record, `send-issued` and the paste run under one wrapper flight lock that the hook claim, turn start/end and wheel moves also take, and a human key never takes it. A paste blocked in the PTY write holds this lock, so the bound limits how long hook events and wheel moves can wait behind it.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** ([PTY] openpty alone; [Human Takeover / Wheel] Windows input retired) — `pty_backend()` is always `openpty`, the pump keeps the input writer until the child exits, and `host_stdin()` is `std::io::stdin()`. The retirement kept «the bridge send as one bracketed write + CR, human bytes held during it» (`decision/atomic-bracketed-send`). That holding is what human keys meet while a paste is blocked or cut, and it is bounded by `decision/human-always-wins-wheel` («never delayed past the current atomic paste»).

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (portable-pty pinned at =0.9.0) — moved the seam to portable-pty `=0.9.0` (`decision/portable-pty-behind-pty-seam`), the seam unchanged. A write timeout has to be built behind viola's own `pty` seam on this pinned version, with no dependency moved.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** — ratified `PtyError` as the one hand-written error, with fixed `Display`/`Error` messages, no thiserror, and the portable-pty error kept only as a boxed source (`decision/pty-error-hand-written`, `decision/pty-knows-no-agent`). A new paste-timeout error in viola-pty follows this form.

**2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize** — gave `decision/human-key-never-held-behind-resize` its Linux reason: no key was lost, so viola adds no wait. This is the latest precedent that the human's keys are never held for a PTY-side condition. It applies to what keys do while a paste is blocked and after it is cut.

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** (the wheel as landed) — the stdin classifier only observes and moves the wheel before a read holding an editing key returns (`decision/wheel-classifier-only-observes`, `decision/wheel-byte-source-claim`). The in-memory move is synchronous and the record and snapshot go on a worker thread. This determines whether a key typed during a blocked paste takes the wheel and whether the cut send reads `human-typing`.

**2026-10-04-running-turn-refusal** — the running-turn state lives in `WheelSlot` and is started by a `prompt-submitted` of any origin. `turn-running` covers a second send in flight, and only `release` of a human-held wheel clears it. This matters for what the next send meets after a cut paste: a still-reserved in-flight slot reads `turn-running`, and a human Enter on the left-over text starts a turn.

The send flight lock: a send cut at the bound releases its flight so the next send is not held behind it.
The bound is compiled: no config key, environment variable or flag sets or switches it off.

body: The paste into the child's PTY ends within a compiled time bound; send never waits on the child's reading without an end.

At the bound the send ends with a closed word: the CLI send result (its --json document, its human line and its exit code) and the MCP send tool result carry that word, never upstream or free text, identical over CLI and MCP.
At the bound the wheel is not moved: a cut paste neither hands the wheel to the human nor records a wheel change.

A new closed word joins the closed refusal, detail or cause sets only by decision, and it passes the MCP reply screen and the CLI human-line screen as a known word, its error body holding no path or upstream text.

The bound's value is read against send's compiled total, the readiness gate's GATE_MAX_WAIT, the send confirmation window and the MCP call deadline (55 s, its expiry call-deadline), so the paste bound plus the rest of send stays under the MCP call deadline and the driver never reads call-deadline for a cut paste.

A cut paste is never presumed delivered: the send's outcome at the bound is not-delivered or unconfirmable as the plan disposes, never confirmed, and the send records and send-issued line say what was written.

What a cut paste leaves in the child's input box (text with no Enter) and what the next send, the human-typing refusal and the send confirmation then meet is disposed in the plan, its choice among priced answers left to the founder's fork.
The send flight lock is released when the paste is cut, so the next send is not held behind a dead paste.
The human is never blocked: the human's keys while a paste is blocked and after it is cut reach the child or are held only as the plan allows, and human input takes the wheel as it does today.
The PTY pump's write contract, its callers and the pump's resize and reader paths keep their behaviour apart from the bounded paste; child exit stays read on the process handle.
The fake agent gains a behaviour, set by argv alone, that stops reading its PTY so its buffer fills; it is a fake-agent command-line option and its receipt lines stay in their format.
The measuring tests run on a real openpty spawn with the fake agent as claude, never a real claude start and no live rig start; a fake-agent run is no proof of real-CLI behaviour.

A test that waits on the bound takes a bound under the 20 s kill line and the root wait bound, below the per-test kills; the CHILD_WITHIN bound stays below the mutants profile kill (now 15 s) and its comment says so.
Where the bound is driven in a unit test, wrapper deadlines go through the injected clock seam; integration tests synchronise on logged events, never sleeps.
The send-refused or send-issued process log line at the bound carries its corr and a code only, no sent text, no secret.
Every test start of viola or a wrapper runs under a test-owned user home with a fresh per-test home, tied in a drop guard.
No mutation run in this chunk; send-window tests keep their mutants kill classes as they stand.
